newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT- T-bonds seen staying choppy within ranges.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- T-bonds seen staying choppy within ranges.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are likely to stay choppy but largely range-bound in the near term, technical analysts said.
The market, which has made a sharp pullback this month after the April-August bull run, appeared to be settling into a more consolidative mode, they said.

"Primarily, what we're looking at is consolidation, and in that scenario you want to be selling resistance and buying support," said David Lundgren, a senior technical analyst at Technical Data. "That's basically been the trade that's worked best in the past three days (after last Friday's nosedive)."

Lundgren saw strong resistance for September T-bond futures at 113-19/32, the high from Tuesday's early spike up which was also where the eight-day moving average and the 200-bar moving average on the 90-minute chart came in.
He said the market might go as high as 113-28/32 but added that that could be "a stretch."
In Thursday's mid-morning business, the September contract was bouncing against a 113-16/32 high it had put in early in the session.
To the downside, Lundgren saw good support at 112-20/32.

David Ging, a Treasury market strategist at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, also expected a few weeks of range-trading and suggested selling bonds near projected resistance and buying them near support.
Ging's upside target was pegged at around 113-31/32, a retracement level, and 114-6/32, the top of a gap on the daytime-only chart.
"I think those are two good levels that will hold at least on the initial test," he said.
He anticipated 111-31/32, the low from Wednesday's rollercoaster ride, to hold near-term.
